title: Grateful Dead Live at West Palm Beach Auditorium on 1982-09-11
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > DAT> CDR

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a high‑energy 1982 show with scorching Let It Grow and an all‑time Scarlet > Fire, despite occasional mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the band’s peak ’82 outings – tight, fiery, and highlighted by standout versions of Let It Grow, Scarlet > Fire, Sailor > Saint and a driving Truckin’/Stella Blue stretch. The soundboard source delivers clear, crisp audio for most of the set, though several listeners note that Jerry’s guitar can dip low while Brent’s keyboards sit forward in the mix.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high ratings (mostly 4‑5 stars) praise both the musical performance and overall sound quality; only occasional mix complaints moderate the score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear for a cassette‑era board tape. Reviewers note occasional level imbalances – Jerry’s guitar sometimes low, Brent’s keyboards heavy – but no major dropouts or distortion.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first set builds into a seamless, high‑energy second set; the Scarlet > Fire transition is frequently called magical.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Fiery, inventive solos praised as "out of his head" and tight throughout; several notes mention his guitar buried low in the mix at times.
band_member_comments.Phil: Laid down a fast, smooth groove especially during Scarlet > Fire; bass work described as solid and tight.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal performances highlighted as strong on tracks like Truckin' and Stella Blue.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s keyboards praised for brilliance and heavy presence in the mix; his interplay with Jerry noted as a highlight.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann deliver tight, energetic drumming with memorable pre‑drum build‑ups.
